title: Operator Chaos Gradebook and Experimentation Handbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview
-------
This handbook defines a standardized, operator-friendly "gradebook" and execution process for platform chaos and resiliency experiments. The goal is to make experiments repeatable, measurable, and actionable so platform teams can continuously improve SLO resilience (latency, availability, token cost) across model-serving subsystems (prefetch/KV cache, batching, routing, fallbacks).

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: platform operators, SREs, runtime engineers, and feature owners.
- Systems covered: KV prefix cache, prefetch cohorts, batching pipeline, model-variant routing, regional failover, tenant isolation.
- Excluded: infra-level hardware failures that require vendor escalation (separate process).

Why a gradebook?
----------------
Operators run many experiments; the gradebook:
- Enforces consistent metrics and severity-weighting
- Produces a single numeric resilience score per experiment
- Stores remediation actions and regression risk for future runbooks

Metrics and scoring rubric
-------------------------
Primary metrics (measured during baseline and during experiment):
- Tail P95/P99 latency (ms) for foreground requests
- Successful token throughput (tokens/sec) per model variant
- Error rate (5xx-equivalent) and silent-fallback counts
- Unit cost delta (USD/token or internal units)
- SLO burn: percent of requests that violated customer-visible SLO in the window

Scoring (0-100): weighted composite where higher is better. Example weights: latency 30, errors 30, throughput 15, cost 15, graceful_degradation 10.

Experiment taxonomy (examples)
-----------------------------
1) Controlled prefetch miss storm
   - Objective: validate cache prefetch admission and operator rollback paths
   - Failure mode: synthetic cohort TTL expiry + cold-prefix surge
2) Batcher head-of-line contention
   - Objective: observe fairness and soft-eviction heuristics under mixed-tenant loads
3) Model-variant cascade
   - Objective: force a primary variant to degrade and verify routing/fallback correctness
4) Regional routing partition
   - Objective: simulate a regional control-plane delay and verify graceful cross-region routing

Pre-experiment checklist (must pass to run in production-sim)
------------------------------------------------------------
1. Stakeholders: assign owner and reviewers, notify oncall rotation.
2. Safety gates: have canary range; define blast radius (tenant subset, region).
3. Monitoring: instrument dashboards and open an experiment run ticket.
4. Automated rollback: pre-configure a playbook to cancel experiment and revert config.
5. Communication plan: Slack channel, Pager duty escalation contact, and expected run window.

Runbook: executing an experiment (step-by-step)
------------------------------------------------
1. Create experiment ticket using template (see Appendix B). Include: hypothesis, blast radius, observability links, rollback steps.
2. Warm baseline: run 30-minute baseline collection at normal traffic to establish priors.
3. Stage 1 (canary): apply failure to 1% of traffic for 10 minutes. Observe metrics and SLI burn.
   - Abort if SLO burn > 5% during canary or unhandled 5xx spike > 2x baseline.
4. Stage 2 (ramp): increase to 10% for 20 minutes. Run gradebook scoring script.
5. Stage 3 (full): expand to full blast radius if Stage 2 passes. Record final grade and remediation notes.
6. Post-run: immediately run smoke check suite and re-collect 30-minute post-recovery baseline.

Abort and rollback criteria (operator checklist)
--------------------------------------------
- Immediate abort triggers: API gateway 5xx > 5% absolute, customer-visible SLO burn > 15%, tenant escalations via support.
- Soft rollback triggers: unexpected long-tail latency increase (P99 > 2x baseline) without throughput benefit.

Dashboards and alert templates
------------------------------
Minimum dashboard panels:
- Real-time SLI panel (P95, P99, error rate) with baseline overlay
- Token throughput per-variant and aggregate cost delta panel
- Operator-gradebook scorecard showing component-level sub-scores (latency/errors/throughput/cost)
- Synthetic canary trace panel showing request scatter and tail examples

Alert rule examples (Prometheus / Alertmanager style):
- name: Experiment_P99_Regression
  expr: increase(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="llm-runtime",quantile="0.99"}[10m]) > (baseline * 2)
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    summary: "P99 regression during chaos experiment: {{ $labels.instance }}"

- name: Gradebook_Score_Drop
  expr: llm_experiment_gradebook_score{experiment="current-run"} < 50
  for: 2m

Postmortem and gradebook entry template
--------------------------------------
Every experiment must create a gradebook entry with these fields (stored in experiment-ticket):
- Experiment ID: string
- Hypothesis: short statement
- Blast radius: tenants/regions/percent traffic
- Run owner: name + pager contact
- Final score: numeric (0-100) and sub-scores per metric
- Observed failures and root cause hypothesis
- Remediation actions and owners (with due dates)
- Regression risk: low/medium/high and why
- Learnings: concrete configuration or code changes planned

Sample gradebook table (rendered):
| Experiment ID | Score | Latency | Errors | Throughput | Cost | Owner | Status |
| EX-2026-321 | 72 | 85/100 | 60/100 | 70/100 | 75/100 | Maya Patel | remediation_open |

Retrospective cadence and template
----------------------------------
- Quarterly deep-dive: aggregate top 5 regressions and follow through on long-lived remediations.
- Post-experiment: short blameless retro within 3 business days with slides covering: hypothesis, what happened, why, next steps.

Roadmap: 6–12 months (prioritized)
--------------------------------
1. Gradebook automation: ingest baseline and compute composite score automatically (Q4 2026).
2. Synthetic runner: scheduling and safe-environment harness to run low-risk regressions nightly (Q1 2027).
3. Cross-team experiment ledger: searchable store for past gradebook entries and owners (Q2 2027).
4. Dashboard library: curated templates for each experiment taxonomy (ongoing).

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Run owner: platform-ops (primary), eng-serving-runtime (secondary)
- Dashboard maintenance: observability team (owner)
- Gradebook storage & tooling: eng-platform infra team

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets
--------------------------------
Create an experiment ticket (CLI):
```
$ rx-ticket create --title "Prefetch miss storm - cohort A" --assignee maya.patel --labels chaos,canary --meta blast_radius=5%
```
Run gradebook scoring script (local):
```
$ python tools/gradebook/compute_score.py --experiment EX-2026-321 --baseline-window 30m --run-window 30m
```
Sample alert JSON for dashboard import (Grafana simplified):
```
{
  "title": "Experiment - SLI Overview",
  "panels": [ { "type": "graph", "targets": [ {"expr":"histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"llm-runtime\"}[5m])) by (le))"} ] } ]
}
```
